status: complete; independently reviewed and locally validated; no commit/push
scope: Shared CPU text intrinsic width, positive first-line indentation and exact-fit wrapping; no shaping or alignment rewrite

change.intrinsic_width: Maximum of each shaped line advance plus its positive first-line paragraph inset; continuation lines add no inset. TextLine.width remains shaped advance.
change.wrap: Compare advance plus first-line positive inset against maximum directly; avoid subtractive f64 cancellation and do not add epsilon.
change.empty_and_negative: Positive-indent empty paragraphs reserve inset width; negative hanging indent retains left overflow and does not increase intrinsic width.
change.resources: No new dependencies, cache, persistent allocations or limits; existing text/glyph/line/outline budgets remain. New production work is scalar arithmetic per line/cluster.
change.unmodified: Shaping, bidi, rich-text segmentation, font fallback, alignment, source text/UTF-16 ranges, GPU pipeline and browser implementation.

reference.method: Use the pinned font to shape the same text with zero indent, then add explicit positive inset to a fixed-width reference. CJK fixtures additionally use independent 20px and 12px advances. Pixel, outline and box-hit comparisons use the fixed reference, not baseline pixels as correctness oracle.

performance.method: Four serialized baseline/candidate rounds after own builds and full test workloads. Same font, fixed inputs, timed functions and loader; each artifact uses a fresh process. Final two rounds additionally record Bun version/executable. 5 warmups,31 samples,4 calls/sample for32 UTF-16 units,1 call/sample for256 units,8 calls/sample for Hug measure. p50=sorted[15],p95=sorted[29], quantiles of batch means; arrays list the initial two then the metadata-confirmed two rounds.
performance.conclusion: Shared-host timings are mixed, with slower cases and substantial p95 variability; these runs do not establish a speed improvement or absence of performance regressions. In the initial rounds the 32-unit zero-indent p50 was 2.43%/2.84% slower and 32-unit negative-indent p95 was 6.03%/136.14% slower. All rounds are retained, including unfavorable samples. Fixed-layout glyphs, spans, bounds and line records retain identical hashes for all 6 sampled cases.
